th: Khi trạng từ phủ định/hạn chế đứng đầu câu, đảo **trợ động từ + chủ ngữ**: Never **have I** seen such a view. Rarely **does he** complain. Seldom **do we** meet.
When a negative or limiting adverbial starts the sentence, invert **auxiliary + subject**: Never **have I** seen such a view. Rarely **does he** complain. Seldom **do we** meet.
**Not only … but (also)**: Not only **did she** win, but she also broke the record.
**Not only … but (also)**: Not only **did she** win, but she also broke the record.

“Vừa … thì”: **No sooner had** + S + V3 **than** …; **Hardly / Scarcely had** + S + V3 **when** …
No sooner had we arrived than it started to rain.

“As soon as”: **No sooner had** + S + V3 **than** …; **Hardly / Scarcely had** + S + V3 **when** …
No sooner had we arrived than it started to rain.
**Only** + thời gian/điều kiện: Only then **did I** realise… Only after the meeting **did he** apologise. **Under no circumstances should** you open this door.
**Only** + time/condition: Only then **did I** realise… Only after the meeting **did he** apologise. **Under no circumstances should** you open this door.
ex: No sooner had we left ___ it began to snow.
Hardly had she arrived ___ the meeting started.
Not only ___ late, but he also forgot the documents.
Only after the test ___ how easy it was.
Under no circumstances you should touch this.
Under no circumstances should you touch this.
Under no circumstances should touch you this.
Rarely does she make a mistake
Hiếm khi cô ấy mắc lỗi.
Seldom have I heard such a convincing argument.

warm.s: No sooner had the speaker finished her presentation than the fire alarm went off and everyone had to leave the building in a hurry.
q: Chuông báo cháy kêu khi nào?
When did the fire alarm go off?
o: Ngay sau khi bài thuyết trình kết thúc
Immediately after the presentation ended
Trước khi bài thuyết trình bắt đầu
Before the presentation started
Giữa bài thuyết trình
In the middle of the presentation
e: No sooner had … than = vừa … thì: hai việc nối tiếp gần như ngay lập tức. Việc thứ nhất (finished) ở quá khứ hoàn thành, việc thứ hai (went off) ở quá khứ đơn.
No sooner had … than = as soon as: one event followed the other immediately. The first (finished) is past perfect, the second (went off) past simple.
f: No sooner had the speaker finished her presentation than

warm.s: Not only did the new manager reduce the team's workload, but she also persuaded the board to raise everyone's salary.
e: Not only đứng đầu → đảo trợ động từ: did the new manager reduce. Vế sau giữ trật tự bình thường: but she also persuaded.
Not only at the start → inversion: did the new manager reduce. The second half keeps normal order: but she also persuaded.
f: Not only did the new manager reduce

warm.s: Under no circumstances should passengers leave their luggage unattended in the terminal, as it may be removed and destroyed by security staff.
e: Nhấn mạnh “no” và “should”; ngắt hơi sau “terminal”. circumstances đọc /ˈsɜː.kəm.stɑːn.sɪz/.
Stress “no” and “should”; pause after “terminal”. circumstances is pronounced /ˈsɜː.kəm.stɑːn.sɪz/.

rd2.tx: Rarely have I stayed in a hotel that promised so much and delivered so little. The photographs on the website showed a spacious room with a sea view; what we actually found was a cramped space overlooking a car park. Not only was the air conditioning broken, but the staff also seemed surprised that anyone would complain about it. No sooner had we unpacked than the noise from a nearby karaoke bar began, and at no point before two in the morning did it stop. Only after I had threatened to post a review online did the manager offer us a different room. To be fair, the breakfast was excellent, and seldom have I tasted better fresh mango. Nevertheless, under no circumstances would I recommend this place to families with young children, nor would I return myself. Little did we know when we booked that the swimming pool had been closed for months.
rd2.tr: Hiếm khi tôi ở một khách sạn hứa hẹn nhiều mà đáp ứng ít đến vậy. Ảnh trên trang web là một căn phòng rộng rãi nhìn ra biển; thực tế chúng tôi nhận được là một chỗ chật chội nhìn ra bãi đỗ xe. Không chỉ điều hòa bị hỏng mà nhân viên còn tỏ ra ngạc nhiên khi có người phàn nàn về chuyện đó. Chúng tôi vừa dỡ đồ ra thì tiếng ồn từ một quán karaoke gần đó bắt đầu, và mãi đến hai giờ sáng nó mới dừng. Chỉ sau khi tôi dọa đăng đánh giá lên mạng thì quản lý mới đổi cho chúng tôi phòng khác. Công bằng mà nói, bữa sáng rất ngon, và hiếm khi tôi được ăn xoài tươi ngon hơn thế. Dù vậy, tôi tuyệt đối không giới thiệu nơi này cho các gia đình có con nhỏ, và bản thân tôi cũng sẽ không quay lại. Lúc đặt phòng, chúng tôi đâu có ngờ bể bơi đã đóng cửa nhiều tháng rồi.

q: Quản lý đổi phòng cho tác giả khi nào?
When did the manager offer a different room?
o: Chỉ sau khi tác giả dọa đăng đánh giá lên mạng
Only after the writer threatened to post an online review
Ngay khi khách vừa đến
As soon as the guests arrived
Sau bữa sáng hôm sau
After breakfast the next day
e: “Only after I had threatened to post a review online did the manager offer us a different room” – Only after + mệnh đề, rồi đảo ngữ did the manager offer.
“Only after I had threatened to post a review online did the manager offer us a different room” – Only after + clause, then inversion did the manager offer.
f: Only after I had threatened to post a review online did the manager offer us a different room

q: Tác giả khen điều gì?
What does the writer praise?
o: Bữa sáng, đặc biệt là xoài tươi
The breakfast, especially the fresh mango
Phòng nhìn ra biển
The sea-view room
Thái độ của nhân viên
The staff's attitude
e: “the breakfast was excellent, and seldom have I tasted better fresh mango” – seldom đứng đầu nên đảo have I. Phòng nhìn ra biển chỉ có trong ảnh quảng cáo.
“the breakfast was excellent, and seldom have I tasted better fresh mango” – seldom first, so have I is inverted. The sea view existed only in the photos.
f: seldom have I tasted better fresh mango

q: Lúc đặt phòng, tác giả không biết điều gì?
What did the writer not know when booking?
o: Bể bơi đã đóng cửa nhiều tháng
The pool had been closed for months
Khách sạn gần quán karaoke
The hotel was near a karaoke bar
Bữa sáng không bao gồm
Breakfast was not included
e: “Little did we know…” = chúng tôi hoàn toàn không biết. Đảo ngữ với little nhấn mạnh sự bất ngờ.
“Little did we know…” = we had no idea. Inversion after little stresses the surprise.
f: Little did we know when we booked that the swimming pool had been closed for months

ex2.s: Seldom ___ such a well-organised conference, with every session starting exactly on time and every speaker staying within the limit.
o: have I attended
I have attended
did I attended
e: Seldom đứng đầu câu → đảo trợ động từ + chủ ngữ: have I attended. “did I attended” sai vì sau did phải là động từ nguyên mẫu.
Seldom at the start → auxiliary + subject inversion: have I attended. “did I attended” is wrong because did needs the base form.

ex2.s: Hardly had the guests sat down at the table ___ the power went off and the whole restaurant was plunged into darkness.
a: when
before
e: Cặp cố định: Hardly / Scarcely had … when (đôi khi before). Bẫy: “than” chỉ đi với No sooner, không đi với Hardly.
Fixed pair: Hardly / Scarcely had … when (sometimes before). Trap: “than” goes only with No sooner, not with Hardly.

ex2.s: Only when the results were published the researchers did realise how serious the mistake in their calculations had been.
a: Only when the results were published did the researchers realise how serious the mistake in their calculations had been.
Only when the results were published did the researchers realize how serious the mistake in their calculations had been.
e: Với Only when + mệnh đề, đảo ngữ xảy ra ở mệnh đề chính: did + chủ ngữ + V (did the researchers realise). Trợ động từ phải đứng trước chủ ngữ.
With Only when + clause, the inversion happens in the main clause: did + subject + verb (did the researchers realise). The auxiliary must come before the subject.

q: Viết lại câu bắt đầu bằng “Not until…”
Rewrite the sentence starting with “Not until…”
ex2.s: I didn't understand how much my parents had sacrificed for my education until I had children of my own.
a: Not until I had children of my own did I understand how much my parents had sacrificed for my education.
Not until I had my own children did I understand how much my parents had sacrificed for my education.
e: Not until + mệnh đề thời gian đưa lên đầu, rồi đảo ở mệnh đề chính: did I understand. Bỏ not trong didn't vì Not until đã mang nghĩa phủ định.
Put Not until + time clause first, then invert the main clause: did I understand. Drop the not of didn't because Not until already carries the negative.

ex2.s: Chúng tôi vừa ra khỏi nhà thì trời bắt đầu mưa như trút nước, nên phải quay lại lấy ô.
a: No sooner had we left the house than it started pouring with rain, so we had to go back for our umbrellas.
No sooner had we left the house than it began to pour, so we had to go back and get our umbrellas.
Hardly had we left the house when it started to pour with rain, so we had to go back for our umbrellas.
Scarcely had we left the house when it began pouring with rain, so we had to go back to get an umbrella.
e: “vừa … thì” → No sooner had + S + V3 + than … hoặc Hardly/Scarcely had … when … Không trộn No sooner với when hay Hardly với than.
“as soon as” → No sooner had + S + past participle + than … or Hardly/Scarcely had … when … Don't mix No sooner with when or Hardly with than.
f: No sooner had we left the house than

ex2.s: Under no circumstances|should you|share your password|with anyone,|even if|they claim|to work for|the bank.
m: Trong bất kỳ hoàn cảnh nào bạn cũng không được chia sẻ mật khẩu cho ai, kể cả khi họ tự nhận là làm cho ngân hàng.
Under no circumstances should you share your password with anyone, even if they claim to work for the bank.
e: Under no circumstances đứng đầu → đảo should you. Cụm này rất hay gặp trong văn bản cảnh báo, hướng dẫn an toàn.
Under no circumstances first → inversion should you. The phrase is common in warnings and safety instructions.

th: **It-cleft** nhấn mạnh một thành phần: It was **Mai** who solved the problem. It is **the price** that worries me.
**It-clefts** highlight one element: It was **Mai** who solved the problem. It is **the price** that worries me.
**What-cleft**: What I need is a long holiday. What surprised me was his reaction. **All** I want is some sleep.
**What-clefts**: What I need is a long holiday. What surprised me was his reaction. **All** I want is some sleep.

**Danh hóa** trong văn học thuật: biến động từ/tính từ thành danh từ để câu trang trọng, cô đọng.
• Prices increased rapidly → There was **a rapid increase** in prices.
• We analysed the data → **Analysis** of the data showed…

**Nominalisation** in academic writing turns verbs/adjectives into nouns for a formal, dense style.
• Prices increased rapidly → There was **a rapid increase** in prices.
• We analysed the data → **Analysis** of the data showed…
ex: It was my grandmother ___ taught me to cook.
___ I like most about Hanoi is the food.
There was a sharp fall in unemployment.
All I want ___ a quiet place to study.
What surprised me was his calm reaction
Điều làm tôi ngạc nhiên là phản ứng bình tĩnh của anh ấy.
There has been a significant increase in investment.

warm.s: What really worried the residents was not the noise from the construction site but the dust that covered their windows every single day.
q: Điều gì làm cư dân lo lắng nhất?
What worried the residents most?
o: Bụi bám cửa sổ mỗi ngày
The dust on their windows every day
Tiếng ồn công trường
The noise from the building site
Công nhân xây dựng
The construction workers
e: Câu chẻ What-cleft nhấn mạnh: “What really worried the residents was … the dust”. Cấu trúc “not X but Y” loại tiếng ồn ra.
The what-cleft highlights “the dust”: “What really worried the residents was … the dust”. “not X but Y” rules out the noise.
f: What really worried the residents was

warm.s: It was only after the third reminder from the bank that he finally decided to deal with his unpaid bills.
e: Câu chẻ It was … that nhấn mạnh thời điểm “only after the third reminder”. Chú ý cụm deal with (giải quyết).
The it-cleft It was … that highlights the time “only after the third reminder”. Note the phrasal verb deal with.
f: It was only after the third reminder from the bank that

warm.s: There has been a significant decline in the number of young people who choose to study agriculture at university over the past decade.
e: Danh hóa: “a significant decline in the number of…”. Nhấn sig-NIF-icant và de-CLINE; đọc nối “decline in”.
Nominalisation: “a significant decline in the number of…”. Stress sig-NIF-i-cant and de-CLINE; link “decline in”.

rd2.tx: The past decade has seen a dramatic increase in the number of private vehicles in Vietnam's largest cities, and with it a steady deterioration in air quality. What concerns health experts most is not the occasional smog that makes headlines, but the long-term exposure of children to fine particles on their daily journey to school. It is this hidden, cumulative damage that is hardest to communicate to the public. A recent analysis of monitoring data showed a clear correlation between traffic density and pollution levels during rush hours. The introduction of low-emission zones, the expansion of metro networks and the electrification of motorbike fleets have all been proposed as solutions. However, the implementation of such measures requires significant investment, and their success depends on public acceptance. What is needed, according to most researchers, is not a single dramatic policy but a combination of gradual changes, supported by clear communication of the benefits.
rd2.tr: Thập kỷ qua chứng kiến sự gia tăng mạnh số lượng phương tiện cá nhân ở các thành phố lớn nhất Việt Nam, kéo theo chất lượng không khí xấu đi đều đặn. Điều khiến các chuyên gia y tế lo ngại nhất không phải là những đợt khói mù thỉnh thoảng lên báo, mà là việc trẻ em phơi nhiễm lâu dài với bụi mịn trên đường đến trường mỗi ngày. Chính tác hại âm thầm, tích tụ này là điều khó truyền đạt tới công chúng nhất. Một phân tích gần đây về dữ liệu quan trắc cho thấy mối tương quan rõ rệt giữa mật độ giao thông và mức ô nhiễm trong giờ cao điểm. Việc lập vùng phát thải thấp, mở rộng mạng lưới tàu điện và điện hóa xe máy đều đã được đề xuất làm giải pháp. Tuy nhiên, việc triển khai những biện pháp này đòi hỏi đầu tư lớn, và thành công của chúng phụ thuộc vào sự đồng thuận của người dân. Theo phần lớn các nhà nghiên cứu, điều cần thiết không phải là một chính sách đột phá duy nhất, mà là sự kết hợp của nhiều thay đổi từ từ, đi kèm việc truyền thông rõ ràng về lợi ích.

q: Điều gì khiến chuyên gia y tế lo ngại nhất?
What concerns health experts most?
o: Trẻ em phơi nhiễm lâu dài với bụi mịn
Children's long-term exposure to fine particles
Những đợt khói mù thỉnh thoảng lên báo
Occasional smog that makes headlines
Giá xe máy điện
The price of electric motorbikes
e: What-cleft: “What concerns health experts most is not the occasional smog…, but the long-term exposure of children…”. Cấu trúc not X but Y cho biết đáp án là Y.
The what-cleft: “What concerns health experts most is not the occasional smog…, but the long-term exposure of children…”. In not X but Y, the answer is Y.
f: the long-term exposure of children to fine particles

q: Phân tích dữ liệu quan trắc cho thấy gì?
What did the analysis of monitoring data show?
o: Mối tương quan giữa mật độ giao thông và mức ô nhiễm giờ cao điểm
A link between traffic density and rush-hour pollution
Ô nhiễm giảm nhờ tàu điện
Pollution fell thanks to the metro
Trẻ em ít đi học bằng xe máy
Fewer children ride to school
e: “A recent analysis of monitoring data showed a clear correlation between traffic density and pollution levels during rush hours.” Chú ý các danh từ hóa: analysis, correlation, density.
“A recent analysis of monitoring data showed a clear correlation between traffic density and pollution levels during rush hours.” Note the nominalisations: analysis, correlation, density.
f: a clear correlation between traffic density and pollution levels

q: Theo các nhà nghiên cứu, điều cần thiết là gì?
According to researchers, what is needed?
o: Kết hợp nhiều thay đổi từ từ
A combination of gradual changes
Một chính sách đột phá duy nhất
One single dramatic policy
Cấm hoàn toàn xe máy
A total ban on motorbikes
e: “What is needed … is not a single dramatic policy but a combination of gradual changes” – lại là What-cleft với not X but Y.
“What is needed … is not a single dramatic policy but a combination of gradual changes” – another what-cleft with not X but Y.

ex2.s: It was the lack of clear communication, rather than the policy itself, ___ caused so much anger among local residents last year.
o: that
what
which
e: Câu chẻ It was + phần nhấn mạnh + that + phần còn lại. what không dùng trong It-cleft; which nghe sai khi phần nhấn mạnh là cả một cụm danh từ trừu tượng như thế này.
An it-cleft is It was + focus + that + the rest. what never appears in an it-cleft, and which sounds wrong after an abstract focus phrase like this.

ex2.s: ___ surprised me most about living abroad was not the food or the weather but how lonely I felt during the first winter.
a: What
e: What-cleft: What + mệnh đề + is/was + phần nhấn mạnh. Không dùng That hay Which ở đầu vì cần một từ mang nghĩa “điều mà”.
A what-cleft: What + clause + is/was + focus. That or Which won't work because you need a word meaning “the thing that”.

ex2.s: What the company needs it is a clear strategy for attracting young talent, not another expensive advertising campaign on television.
a: What the company needs is a clear strategy for attracting young talent, not another expensive advertising campaign on television.
e: Mệnh đề What the company needs đã là chủ ngữ, nên không thêm it nữa. Lỗi này xuất hiện do dịch sát cấu trúc “Điều công ty cần, đó là…”.
The clause What the company needs is already the subject, so don't add it. The mistake comes from translating “Điều công ty cần, đó là…” word for word.

q: Danh hóa: viết lại câu bắt đầu bằng “There was a sharp…”
Nominalise: rewrite the sentence starting with “There was a sharp…”
ex2.s: The number of international students who applied to Vietnamese universities increased sharply after the new visa rules were introduced.
a: There was a sharp increase in the number of international students applying to Vietnamese universities after the introduction of the new visa rules.
There was a sharp increase in the number of international students who applied to Vietnamese universities after the new visa rules were introduced.
There was a sharp increase in the number of international students applying to Vietnamese universities after the new visa rules were introduced.
There was a sharp rise in the number of international students applying to Vietnamese universities after the introduction of the new visa rules.
e: increased sharply → a sharp increase in (trạng từ thành tính từ, động từ thành danh từ + in). Có thể danh hóa tiếp: were introduced → the introduction of.
increased sharply → a sharp increase in (adverb becomes adjective, verb becomes noun + in). You can go further: were introduced → the introduction of.
f: a sharp increase in the number of

ex2.s: Điều tôi cần nhất lúc này không phải là thêm lời khuyên, mà là một chút thời gian để suy nghĩ cho thấu đáo.
a: What I need most right now is not more advice but a little time to think things through.
What I need most at the moment is not more advice but some time to think it through properly.
What I need most now isn't more advice, but a bit of time to think things over carefully.
What I need most right now is not more advice, but a little time to think things through carefully.
e: “Điều tôi cần nhất” → What-cleft: What I need most is… advice không đếm được nên nói more advice, không nói “more advices”.
“The thing I need most” → a what-cleft: What I need most is… advice is uncountable, so say more advice, never “more advices”.

ex2.s: The rapid expansion|of the metro network|has led to|a significant reduction|in traffic congestion|in the city centre|during rush hour.
m: Việc mở rộng nhanh mạng lưới tàu điện đã giúp giảm đáng kể tình trạng tắc đường ở trung tâm thành phố vào giờ cao điểm.
The rapid expansion of the metro network has led to a significant reduction in traffic congestion in the city centre during rush hour.
e: Hai cụm danh hóa: The rapid expansion of… (thay cho “the metro network expanded rapidly”) và a significant reduction in… Nhớ giới từ: expansion of, reduction in.
Two nominalisations: The rapid expansion of… (instead of “the metro network expanded rapidly”) and a significant reduction in… Remember the prepositions: expansion of, reduction in.

th:
**Ngữ pháp 1 – văn phong email trang trọng**
• Mở đầu: Dear Mr Lee / Dear Ms Taylor, Thank you for your email of 3 May.
• Gửi kèm: Please find attached our quotation. (không viết “I send you …”)
• Đề nghị: Should you require any further information, please do not hesitate to contact me.
• Kết thư: I look forward to hearing from you. / Yours sincerely (biết tên), Yours faithfully (không biết tên – Anh–Anh).

**Grammar 1 – formal email style**
• Opening: Dear Mr Lee / Dear Ms Taylor, Thank you for your email of 3 May.
• Attachments: Please find attached our quotation. (not “I send you …”)
• Offers: Should you require any further information, please do not hesitate to contact me.
• Closing: I look forward to hearing from you. / Yours sincerely (name known), Yours faithfully (name unknown – British).

**Ngữ pháp 2 – câu điều kiện loại 2 khi đàm phán**
• If + quá khứ đơn, would/could + V: If you doubled the order, we would offer free delivery.
• Mềm hơn: If you were able to pay in advance, we could reduce the price by 3%.
• Điều kiện chặt chẽ: provided that / as long as + hiện tại: We can extend the terms provided that the contract is signed this month.
• Loại 2 nghe “giả định” nên lịch sự hơn loại 1 – đối tác thấy có chỗ thương lượng.

**Grammar 2 – second conditional in negotiation**
• If + past simple, would/could + verb: If you doubled the order, we would offer free delivery.
• Softer: If you were able to pay in advance, we could reduce the price by 3%.
• Firm conditions: provided that / as long as + present: We can extend the terms provided that the contract is signed this month.
• The second conditional sounds hypothetical, so it is more polite and leaves room to negotiate.

**Phát âm – trọng âm đổi theo từ loại**
• **CON**tract (danh từ: hợp đồng) – con**TRACT** (động từ: co lại, ký hợp đồng).
• **IN**crease (danh từ) – in**CREASE** (động từ); **RE**cord – re**CORD**; **PRO**duce – pro**DUCE**.
• Ví dụ: We signed the **CON**tract. / Prices will in**CREASE** next year.

**Pronunciation – stress shifts with word class**
• **CON**tract (noun) – con**TRACT** (verb).
• **IN**crease (noun) – in**CREASE** (verb); **RE**cord – re**CORD**; **PRO**duce – pro**DUCE**.
• Examples: We signed the **CON**tract. / Prices will in**CREASE** next year.

**Tự luyện ngoài app**
• Nghe (30 phút): nghe 1 đoạn đàm phán mẫu, ghi đề nghị ban đầu, điều kiện nhượng bộ và kết quả cuối.
• Nói (30 phút): đóng vai người mua – người bán thương lượng giá, số lượng, thời hạn giao hàng (3 vòng đề nghị).
• Đọc (30 phút): đọc 1 hợp đồng mẫu ngắn, tóm tắt 5 điều khoản chính bằng tiếng Việt.
• Viết (50 phút): viết 3 email trang trọng 120–150 từ: gửi báo giá, đề nghị giảm giá, xác nhận đơn hàng.
• Từ vựng (20 phút): lập bảng 10 cụm mở đầu và kết thúc email trang trọng.
• Thử thách: quay video 60 giây giới thiệu (pitch) một sản phẩm: vấn đề, giải pháp, giá, lời kêu gọi hành động; xem lại và quay lần 2.

**Practice outside the app**
• Listening (30 min): listen to a sample negotiation; note the first offer, the concessions and the final result.
• Speaking (30 min): role-play buyer and seller negotiating price, quantity and delivery time (3 rounds of offers).
• Reading (30 min): read a short sample contract and summarise 5 key terms in Vietnamese.
• Writing (50 min): write 3 formal emails of 120–150 words: sending a quotation, asking for a discount, confirming an order.
• Vocabulary (20 min): make a table of 10 formal email openings and closings.
• Challenge: film a 60-second product pitch (problem, solution, price, call to action), watch it and film it again.

Question: What makes a good negotiator? – Model answer. “walk-away point” = the minimum you will accept.

Question: Is it better to work for a big company or start your own business? – Model answer. Link “own_business”.

Honestly, that price is a little over our budget – could you come down a bit if we signed a two-year contract?
To be honest, that price is a bit over our budget. Could you meet us halfway if we signed a two-year contract?

We would appreciate it if you could send us the signed contract by Friday at the latest.

hard.s: The client said that they will consider our offer, but only if we could guarantee delivery before the end of the month.

e: Câu tường thuật lùi thì: will → would, khớp với “could” phía sau.

hard.s: After three hours of negotiation, we finally managed to strike a ___ that kept both sides happy and protected our profit margin.

balance

Dear Ms Taylor,

Thank you for your email of 3 May and for your interest in our bamboo furniture. Please find attached our updated quotation for the 800 chairs and 200 tables you requested.

As discussed during our call, the prices include delivery to your warehouse in Rotterdam but do not include import tax. We understand that your budget is tight this year. However, if you were able to increase your order to more than 1,000 units, we would be prepared to offer a 5% discount. We could also extend the payment terms from 30 to 60 days, provided that the contract is signed by the end of this month.

Regarding delivery, we can ship the goods within six weeks of receiving your deposit. Should you require any changes to the terms, please do not hesitate to contact me. We value our partnership and are confident that this agreement would be profitable for both sides.

I look forward to hearing from you.

Yours sincerely,
Tran Quoc Bao
Sales Director, Viet Bamboo Company
rd2.tr:
Kính gửi bà Taylor,

Cảm ơn bà về email ngày 3 tháng 5 và sự quan tâm đến đồ nội thất tre của chúng tôi. Chúng tôi xin gửi kèm báo giá cập nhật cho 800 chiếc ghế và 200 chiếc bàn mà bà yêu cầu.

Như đã trao đổi trong cuộc gọi, giá đã bao gồm giao hàng đến kho của bà ở Rotterdam nhưng chưa bao gồm thuế nhập khẩu. Chúng tôi hiểu rằng năm nay ngân sách của bà khá eo hẹp. Tuy nhiên, nếu bà có thể tăng đơn hàng lên hơn 1.000 sản phẩm, chúng tôi sẵn sàng chiết khấu 5%. Chúng tôi cũng có thể kéo dài thời hạn thanh toán từ 30 lên 60 ngày, với điều kiện hợp đồng được ký trước cuối tháng này.

Về giao hàng, chúng tôi có thể gửi hàng trong vòng sáu tuần kể từ khi nhận tiền đặt cọc. Nếu bà cần thay đổi điều khoản nào, xin đừng ngần ngại liên hệ với tôi. Chúng tôi trân trọng mối quan hệ đối tác và tin rằng thỏa thuận này sẽ mang lại lợi nhuận cho cả hai bên.

Mong sớm nhận được phản hồi của bà.

Trân trọng,
Trần Quốc Bảo

e: Câu điều kiện loại 2: If + quá khứ đơn (doubled), would + V. Không dùng “double” hay “will double”.

e: Cụm cố định “Please find attached …”. Không viết “attach” hay “attachment”.

a: hearing
e: “to” trong “look forward to” là giới từ → V-ing: hearing. Lỗi phổ biến: “look forward to hear”.
The “to” in “look forward to” is a preposition → -ing: hearing. Common mistake: “look forward to hear”.

ex2.s: We ___ be able to lower the unit price by three percent if you agreed to pay half of the total amount in advance.
o: would
will
are
e: Mệnh đề if dùng quá khứ (agreed) → câu điều kiện loại 2 → would. “will” chỉ đi với if + hiện tại.
The if-clause uses the past (agreed) → second conditional → would. “will” goes with if + present.
f: would be able to lower the unit price

ex2.s: We are writing to confirm that the goods will be delivered within six weeks, providing that you will pay the deposit by Monday.
a: We are writing to confirm that the goods will be delivered within six weeks, provided that you pay the deposit by Monday.
We are writing to confirm that the goods will be delivered within six weeks, providing that you pay the deposit by Monday.
e: Sau provided/providing that dùng hiện tại đơn cho tương lai (you pay), không dùng “will pay” – giống mệnh đề if.
After provided/providing that, use the present simple for the future (you pay), not “will pay” – just like an if-clause.
f: provided that you pay the deposit

q: Viết lại câu cho trang trọng, bắt đầu bằng “Should …” (đảo ngữ thay cho If).
Rewrite formally, starting with “Should …” (inversion instead of If).
ex2.s: If you have any questions about the contract, please do not hesitate to contact me directly.
a: Should you have any questions about the contract, please do not hesitate to contact me directly.
e: Đảo ngữ trang trọng: Should + chủ ngữ + động từ nguyên mẫu = If … . Bỏ “If”, động từ “have” giữ nguyên.
Formal inversion: Should + subject + base verb = If … . Drop “If”; “have” stays in the base form.

ex2.s: Chúng tôi có thể giao hàng trong vòng 2 tuần.
a: We can deliver within two weeks.
We can deliver within 2 weeks.
We can deliver the goods within two weeks.
We are able to deliver within two weeks.
e: “within two weeks” = trong vòng 2 tuần (không quá). “in two weeks” lại có nghĩa là sau 2 tuần nữa.
“within two weeks” = no more than two weeks. “in two weeks” means two weeks from now.

ex2.s: Giá này đã bao gồm thuế chưa?
a: Does this price include tax?
Does the price include tax?
Is tax included in this price?
Is this price inclusive of tax?
e: Dùng “Does … include …?”; hoặc bị động “Is tax included …?”. Không viết “Is this price include tax?”.
Use “Does … include …?” or the passive “Is tax included …?”. Not “Is this price include tax?”.

ex2.s: Chúng tôi rất tiếc phải thông báo rằng lô hàng sẽ bị chậm khoảng một tuần do thiếu nguyên liệu.
a: We regret to inform you that the shipment will be delayed by about a week due to a shortage of materials.
We regret to inform you that the shipment will be delayed by around one week due to a shortage of raw materials.
We are sorry to inform you that the shipment will be delayed by about a week because of a shortage of materials.
We regret to inform you that the delivery will be delayed by approximately one week owing to a shortage of materials.
e: “We regret to inform you that …” mở đầu tin xấu trang trọng; “be delayed by” + thời gian; “due to/owing to” + danh từ.
“We regret to inform you that …” formally introduces bad news; “be delayed by” + time; “due to/owing to” + noun.
f: We regret to inform you that

ex2.s: We would be prepared|to extend the payment terms|to sixty days|as long as|the first order|is confirmed|before the end of the quarter
m: Chúng tôi sẵn sàng kéo dài thời hạn thanh toán lên 60 ngày miễn là đơn hàng đầu tiên được xác nhận trước cuối quý.
We would be prepared to extend the payment terms to sixty days as long as the first order is confirmed before the end of the quarter.
e: “would be prepared to” = sẵn sàng (lịch sự); “as long as” + hiện tại đơn bị động “is confirmed”.
“would be prepared to” = would be willing to (polite); “as long as” + present simple passive “is confirmed”.
f: as long as the first order is confirmed

q: Viết email khoảng 150 từ trả lời khách hàng phàn nàn giao hàng trễ: xin lỗi, giải thích, đề nghị bồi thường, giữ quan hệ.
Write an email (about 150 words) replying to a client who complains about late delivery: apologise, explain, offer compensation and keep the relationship.
ex2.m:
Dear Mr Lee,

Thank you for your email of 14 October regarding the late delivery of your order no. 2381. Please accept our sincere apologies for the inconvenience this has caused your business.

The delay was the result of a serious storm in central Vietnam, which closed the port in Da Nang for four days. Although this was beyond our control, we fully understand how important punctual delivery is to your customers.

As a gesture of goodwill, we would like to offer you a 10% discount on this order and free express shipping on your next two orders. In addition, we have arranged a second shipping route so that similar delays should not happen again.

We greatly value our partnership and hope that this solution is acceptable to you. Should you have any further questions, please do not hesitate to contact me directly.

I look forward to hearing from you.

Yours sincerely,
Nguyen Minh Chau
Customer Relations Manager
e: Cần có: lời xin lỗi trang trọng; lý do rõ ràng; đề nghị bồi thường cụ thể (giảm giá, miễn phí vận chuyển); cam kết cho tương lai + câu kết giữ quan hệ.
Include: a formal apology; a clear reason; concrete compensation (discount, free shipping); a promise for the future + a closing that protects the relationship.

th:
**Ngữ pháp 1 – Ngôn ngữ nghĩa vụ & quyền (văn phong trang trọng)**
• **be required / obliged to + V**: có nghĩa vụ: Landlords **are required to** return deposits within 14 days.
• **be entitled to + danh từ / V**: có quyền (được hưởng): You **are entitled to** paid leave.
• **be liable for + danh từ / V-ing**: chịu trách nhiệm pháp lý: Tenants **are liable for** any damage. (≠ **be liable to + V** = có khả năng: Prices are liable to change.)
• **be prohibited from + V-ing**: bị cấm: Tenants **are prohibited from** subletting.
• Sắc thái: **must** (mạnh, người nói áp đặt) – **have to** (quy định bên ngoài) – **be obliged to** (trang trọng, pháp lý).

**Grammar 1 – Language of obligation & rights (formal register)**
• **be required / obliged to + verb**: have a duty: Landlords **are required to** return deposits within 14 days.
• **be entitled to + noun / verb**: have a right: You **are entitled to** paid leave.
• **be liable for + noun / -ing**: legally responsible: Tenants **are liable for** any damage. (≠ **be liable to + verb** = likely to: Prices are liable to change.)
• **be prohibited from + -ing**: forbidden: Tenants **are prohibited from** subletting.
• Nuance: **must** (strong, speaker's authority) – **have to** (external rule) – **be obliged to** (formal, legal).

**Ngữ pháp 2 – Đảo ngữ & lịch sự mà cứng rắn**
• Đảo ngữ phủ định: **Under no circumstances does** the agreement allow… / **Not only did** they refuse…, but…
• Điều kiện trang trọng: **Should I not hear** from you by Friday, … (= If I don't hear…)
• Giảm nhẹ trước khi phản đối: **I appreciate that** you may have been busy; **however, I must point out that**…
• Leo thang lịch sự: **I would prefer to resolve this amicably** (ngụ ý: nếu không, tôi sẽ đi tiếp) → **I will have no choice but to**…
• Bảng sắc thái: “sort it out” (thân mật) – “deal with it” (trung tính) – “resolve / address the matter” (trang trọng).

**Grammar 2 – Inversion & being polite but firm**
• Negative inversion: **Under no circumstances does** the agreement allow… / **Not only did** they refuse…, but…
• Formal conditional: **Should I not hear** from you by Friday, … (= If I don't hear…)
• Soften before disagreeing: **I appreciate that** you may have been busy; **however, I must point out that**…
• Polite escalation: **I would prefer to resolve this amicably** (implied: otherwise I will go further) → **I will have no choice but to**…
• Register scale: “sort it out” (informal) – “deal with it” (neutral) – “resolve / address the matter” (formal).

**Phát âm – Trọng âm danh từ / động từ**
• Danh từ nhấn âm 1, động từ nhấn âm 2: **CON**tract – con**TRACT**, **RE**cord – re**CORD**, **OB**ject – ob**JECT**, **PER**mit – per**MIT**, **CON**duct – con**DUCT**.
• Trong email đọc to/cuộc gọi chính thức: nói chậm, ngắt nhịp trước “however”, nhấn từ then chốt: I **MUST** point out…
• liable /ˈlaɪ.ə.bəl/, entitled /ɪnˈtaɪ.t̬əld/, clause /klɑːz/.

**Pronunciation – Noun / verb stress**
• Nouns stress the first syllable, verbs the second: **CON**tract – con**TRACT**, **RE**cord – re**CORD**, **OB**ject – ob**JECT**, **PER**mit – per**MIT**, **CON**duct – con**DUCT**.
• On a formal call: speak slowly, pause before “however”, stress the key word: I **MUST** point out…
• liable /ˈlaɪ.ə.bəl/, entitled /ɪnˈtaɪ.t̬əld/, clause /klɑːz/.

**Tự luyện ngoài app**
• Nghe (30 phút): nghe 1 tập podcast/chương trình tư vấn pháp lý cho người tiêu dùng, ghi các cụm “you're entitled to / they're obliged to”.
• Nói (25 phút): đóng vai gọi điện khiếu nại (đổi hàng lỗi, tiền cọc) – lần 1 thân mật, lần 2 trang trọng; so sánh.
• Đọc (30 phút): đọc điều khoản của 1 hợp đồng thuê nhà/điều khoản dịch vụ, liệt kê 5 nghĩa vụ và 5 quyền.
• Viết (40 phút): viết email khiếu nại 150–180 từ: lịch sự – nêu căn cứ – yêu cầu cụ thể – hạn chót.
• Từ vựng (15 phút): học cặp gần nghĩa: right/entitlement, obliged/required, sue/take legal action, breach/violate.

**Practice outside the app**
• Listening (30 min): listen to a consumer-rights podcast or radio phone-in and note “you're entitled to / they're obliged to”.
• Speaking (25 min): role-play a complaint call (faulty product, deposit) – first informal, then formal; compare.
• Reading (30 min): read a tenancy agreement or terms of service and list 5 obligations and 5 rights.
• Writing (40 min): write a 150–180-word complaint email: polite – give grounds – specific request – deadline.
• Vocabulary (15 min): learn near-synonyms: right/entitlement, obliged/required, sue/take legal action, breach/violate.

rd2.tx:
Dear Mr Hall,
I am writing regarding the return of my deposit for the flat at 12 River Street, which I vacated on 30 June. According to clause 7 of our tenancy agreement, you are required to return the deposit within fourteen days unless there is damage beyond normal wear and tear. Six weeks have now passed, and I have yet to receive either the money or an explanation.
I appreciate that you may have been busy, and I would prefer to resolve this matter amicably. However, I must point out that under no circumstances does the agreement entitle you to deduct cleaning costs, as the flat was professionally cleaned before I left; I have attached the receipt and photographs taken on the day.
I would therefore be grateful if you could transfer the full amount by 15 August. Should I not hear from you by then, I will have no choice but to refer the matter to the deposit protection scheme.
I look forward to your prompt reply.
Yours sincerely,
Lan Nguyen

th:
**Ngữ pháp 1 – Từ nối nguyên nhân/kết quả & đối lập theo văn phong**
• Nguyên nhân + danh từ: **owing to / due to / as a result of** (trang trọng) – **because of** (trung tính) – **thanks to** (thường mang nghĩa tích cực, hoặc mỉa mai).
• Kết quả: **consequently / as a consequence** (trang trọng); **thereby + V-ing**: The firm cut prices, **thereby attracting** new customers.
• Đối lập: **whereas** (so sánh hai vế), **despite / in spite of + danh từ/V-ing**, **although + mệnh đề**.
• Danh từ hoá (văn phong học thuật): *The company expanded rapidly* → **The company's rapid expansion** resulted in…

**Grammar 1 – Cause/effect & contrast linkers by register**
• Cause + noun: **owing to / due to / as a result of** (formal) – **because of** (neutral) – **thanks to** (usually positive, or ironic).
• Result: **consequently / as a consequence** (formal); **thereby + -ing**: The firm cut prices, **thereby attracting** new customers.
• Contrast: **whereas** (comparing two sides), **despite / in spite of + noun/-ing**, **although + clause**.
• Nominalisation (formal style): *The company expanded rapidly* → **The company's rapid expansion** resulted in…

**Tranh luận & thuyết phục (ngữ dụng)**
• Nhượng bộ rồi phản bác: **I take your point, but surely…** / **Agreed – in principle. In practice, however, …**
• Phản đối lịch sự: **With respect, that's only half the picture.** (ngụ ý: anh nói đúng một phần nhưng thiếu)
• Câu hỏi tu từ: **Isn't that worth defending?** (không cần trả lời – để thuyết phục).
• Thành ngữ: **a double-edged sword** (con dao hai lưỡi), **a level playing field** (sân chơi bình đẳng), **the bottom line** (điều cốt lõi), **turn your back on** (quay lưng với).
• Gần nghĩa: **economic** (thuộc kinh tế) / **economical** (tiết kiệm) / **economics** (môn kinh tế học); **rise** (tự tăng) / **raise** (làm tăng); **affect** (động từ) / **effect** (danh từ).

**Debating & persuading (pragmatics)**
• Concede, then counter: **I take your point, but surely…** / **Agreed – in principle. In practice, however, …**
• Polite disagreement: **With respect, that's only half the picture.** (implied: you're partly right but incomplete)
• Rhetorical question: **Isn't that worth defending?** (no answer expected – it persuades).
• Idioms: **a double-edged sword**, **a level playing field**, **the bottom line**, **turn your back on**.
• Near-synonyms: **economic** (about the economy) / **economical** (saving money) / **economics** (the subject); **rise** (go up) / **raise** (make go up); **affect** (verb) / **effect** (noun).

**Phát âm – Trọng âm & ngữ điệu tranh luận**
• e**CON**omy – eco**NOM**ic – e**CON**omist; **GLO**bal – globali**SA**tion; multi**NA**tional.
• Liệt kê: lên giọng ở các mục trước, xuống giọng ở mục cuối: jobs ↗, investment ↗ and cheaper goods ↘.
• Nhấn tương phản: In **PRIN**ciple, yes. In **PRAC**tice, no.
• Câu hỏi tu từ xuống giọng ở cuối (khác câu hỏi thật).

**Pronunciation – Stress & debating intonation**
• e**CON**omy – eco**NOM**ic – e**CON**omist; **GLO**bal – globali**SA**tion; multi**NA**tional.
• Lists: rise on the earlier items, fall on the last: jobs ↗, investment ↗ and cheaper goods ↘.
• Contrastive stress: In **PRIN**ciple, yes. In **PRAC**tice, no.
• Rhetorical questions fall at the end (unlike real questions).

**Tự luyện ngoài app**
• Nghe (30 phút): nghe 1 đoạn tranh luận/podcast kinh tế, ghi lại các câu nhượng bộ – phản bác (I take your point, but…).
• Nói (30 phút): tự tranh luận 2 phút ủng hộ rồi 2 phút phản đối “Mua hàng nội tốt hơn hàng ngoại”.
• Đọc (30 phút): đọc 1 bài báo kinh tế, gạch chân từ nối nguyên nhân – kết quả và cụm danh từ hoá.
• Viết (40 phút): viết bài phát biểu mở đầu 150–180 từ cho một cuộc tranh luận, dùng 1 câu hỏi tu từ và 2 thành ngữ.
• Từ vựng (15 phút): học cặp dễ nhầm: economic/economical, rise/raise, affect/effect, cheap/affordable.

**Practice outside the app**
• Listening (30 min): listen to a debate or economics podcast and note concede-and-counter phrases (I take your point, but…).

t: Thành ngữ & cách nói tự nhiên
th:
**Ngữ pháp 1 – Thành ngữ là “khối cố định”**
• Không thay từ, không đổi số ít/nhiều, không thêm/bớt mạo từ: **a piece of cake** (KHÔNG “a slice of cake”), **jump to conclusions** (luôn số nhiều), **cut corners** (KHÔNG “cut the corners”).
• Nhưng **động từ vẫn chia thì** và **đại từ thay đổi**: We **bit off** more than **we could** chew. / She's **gone the extra mile**. / Stop **beating around the bush**.
• Nghĩa đen ≠ nghĩa thật: **under the weather** không phải “dưới thời tiết” mà = hơi ốm; **a blessing in disguise** = trong cái rủi có cái may.

**Grammar 1 – Idioms are “fixed blocks”**
• Don't change the words, the singular/plural or the articles: **a piece of cake** (NOT “a slice of cake”), **jump to conclusions** (always plural), **cut corners** (NOT “cut the corners”).
• But **verbs still change tense** and **pronouns change**: We **bit off** more than **we could** chew. / She's **gone the extra mile**. / Stop **beating around the bush**.
• Literal ≠ real meaning: **under the weather** has nothing to do with the sky – it means slightly ill; **a blessing in disguise** = something bad that turns out to be good.

**Ngữ pháp 2 – Nghĩa đen vs hàm ý trong hội thoại thật**
• “Can I **address the elephant in the room**?” = Tôi xin nói thẳng vấn đề ai cũng biết mà né tránh.
• “It's **not really my cup of tea**.” = Tôi không thích lắm (cách từ chối mềm, không chê).
• “Let's **call it a day**.” = Hôm nay dừng ở đây nhé.
• So sánh 3 cách nói cùng một ý: “We tried to do too much.” (trung tính) → “We **bit off more than we could chew**.” (tự nhiên, thân mật) → “The project was **overly ambitious** in scope.” (trang trọng, văn bản).
• Thành ngữ chủ yếu dùng khi **nói và viết thân mật/trung tính**; trong báo cáo, thư trang trọng nên hạn chế. Dùng 1–2 cái “đắt” hay hơn nhồi 6 cái vào một đoạn.

**Grammar 2 – Literal meaning vs implication in real conversation**
• “Can I **address the elephant in the room**?” = Let me mention the obvious problem everyone is avoiding.
• “It's **not really my cup of tea**.” = I don't like it much (a soft way to say no without criticising).
• “Let's **call it a day**.” = Let's stop here for today.
• The same idea in 3 styles: “We tried to do too much.” (neutral) → “We **bit off more than we could chew**.” (natural, informal) → “The project was **overly ambitious** in scope.” (formal, written).
• Idioms belong mainly to **speech and informal/neutral writing**; use them sparingly in reports and formal letters. One or two well-chosen idioms beat six crammed into one paragraph.

**Thành ngữ tiếng Việt ↔ tiếng Anh (gần nghĩa, không dịch từng chữ)**
• Một công đôi việc ↔ **kill two birds with one stone**
• Nước đến chân mới nhảy ↔ **leave things to the last minute**
• Trong cái rủi có cái may ↔ **a blessing in disguise**
• Vẽ đường cho hươu chạy ↔ **give someone ideas**
• Nói vòng vo tam quốc ↔ **beat around the bush**
• Năm thì mười họa ↔ **once in a blue moon**
• Chuyện cũ bỏ qua ↔ **let bygones be bygones**

**Vietnamese ↔ English idioms (close meaning, not word-for-word)**
• Một công đôi việc ↔ **kill two birds with one stone**
• Nước đến chân mới nhảy ↔ **leave things to the last minute**

• Vẽ đường cho hươu chạy ↔ **give someone ideas**
• Nói vòng vo tam quốc ↔ **beat around the bush**
• Năm thì mười họa ↔ **once in a blue moon**
• Chuyện cũ bỏ qua ↔ **let bygones be bygones**

**Phát âm – Đọc thành ngữ như MỘT cụm**
• Nối âm, không ngắt giữa chừng: piece‿of cake /ˌpiːs‿əv ˈkeɪk/, cut‿corners, call‿it‿a day /ˌkɑːl‿ɪɾ‿ə ˈdeɪ/.
• Trọng âm rơi vào **từ nội dung cuối**: under the **WEA**ther, once in a blue **MOON**, hit the nail on the **HEAD**.
• Từ chức năng đọc yếu: of /əv/, the /ðə/, a /ə/ – nếu đọc rõ từng từ, thành ngữ nghe như đang “đọc sách”.

**Pronunciation – Say an idiom as ONE chunk**
• Link the words, no pauses inside: piece‿of cake /ˌpiːs‿əv ˈkeɪk/, cut‿corners, call‿it‿a day /ˌkɑːl‿ɪɾ‿ə ˈdeɪ/.
• The main stress falls on the **last content word**: under the **WEA**ther, once in a blue **MOON**, hit the nail on the **HEAD**.
• Function words are weak: of /əv/, the /ðə/, a /ə/ – pronouncing every word fully makes an idiom sound “read from a book”.

• Nghe (25 phút): xem 1 tập sitcom/podcast đời thường, ghi lại 5 thành ngữ và đoán nghĩa từ ngữ cảnh trước khi tra.
• Nói (20 phút): kể 2 phút về một sự kiện bạn từng tổ chức, dùng tự nhiên 3 thành ngữ (bit off more than…, a blessing in disguise, call it a day).
• Đọc (20 phút): đọc 1 bài báo phong cách đời sống (lifestyle), gạch chân thành ngữ và phân loại: thân mật / trung tính.
• Viết (30 phút): viết tin nhắn nhóm 120–150 từ rủ hàng xóm làm tình nguyện, dùng tối đa 4 thành ngữ.
• Từ vựng (15 phút): làm thẻ “nghĩa đen ↔ nghĩa thật ↔ thành ngữ Việt tương đương” cho 10 thành ngữ của bài.

**Practice outside the app**
• Listening (25 min): watch a sitcom episode or everyday podcast, note 5 idioms and guess their meaning from context before checking.
• Speaking (20 min): talk for 2 minutes about an event you once organised, naturally using 3 idioms (bit off more than…, a blessing in disguise, call it a day).
• Reading (20 min): read a lifestyle article, underline the idioms and label them informal / neutral.
• Writing (30 min): write a 120–150-word group message inviting neighbours to volunteer, using no more than 4 idioms.
• Vocabulary (15 min): make “literal ↔ real meaning ↔ Vietnamese equivalent” cards for the 10 idioms in this unit.

warm.s: Karaoke isn't really my cup of tea, but I went to the party anyway because my neighbours had gone the extra mile to organise it.
q: Vì sao người nói vẫn đi dự tiệc?
Why did the speaker go to the party?
o: Vì hàng xóm đã rất cất công tổ chức
Because the neighbours had made a big effort to organise it
Vì người nói rất thích hát karaoke
Because the speaker loves karaoke
Vì bữa tiệc được tổ chức ngay gần nhà
Because the party was very close to home
e: “not really my cup of tea” = không thích lắm, nên phương án 2 sai; lý do thật nằm ở “had gone the extra mile” = đã cố gắng hơn mức bình thường.
“not really my cup of tea” = I don't like it much, so option 2 is wrong; the real reason is “had gone the extra mile” = made a special effort.

warm.s: Let's not beat around the bush: we bit off more than we could chew last year, and we can't afford to make the same mistake again.
e: Chú ý: **beat around the bush** (bush số ít), **bit off** (quá khứ của bite off), **could chew** (lùi thì theo bit).
Note: **beat around the bush** (singular bush), **bit off** (past of bite off), **could chew** (backshifted to match bit).
f: bit off more than we could chew

warm.s: Losing the sponsor turned out to be a blessing in disguise, because it forced us to keep the festival small, local and friendly.
e: Đọc “a blessing in disguise” liền một hơi, nhấn **BLESS**ing và dis**GUISE**; liệt kê “small, local and friendly” lên giọng ở 2 từ đầu, xuống ở từ cuối.
Say “a blessing in disguise” as one chunk, stressing **BLESS**ing and dis**GUISE**; in the list, rise on the first two items and fall on the last.

warm.s: Before we get the ball rolling, I just want to make sure that everyone is on the same page about the budget and the deadline.
e: Nối âm get‿the ball, on‿the same page; nhấn **ROLL**ing và **PAGE**. “just” đọc nhẹ để câu nghe lịch sự.
Link get‿the ball and on‿the same page; stress **ROLL**ing and **PAGE**. Keep “just” light to sound polite.

hard.s: Thôi, chuyện cũ bỏ qua đi – hai đứa mình chơi với nhau mười năm rồi, không đáng để giận nhau vì mấy chuyện vặt vãnh như vậy đâu.
a: Let's just let bygones be bygones – we've been friends for ten years, and it's not worth falling out over something so trivial.
Come on, let's let bygones be bygones – we've been friends for ten years, so it's really not worth falling out over such a small thing.
Let's put it behind us – we've been friends for ten years, and it's not worth falling out over something so petty.
Let's just let bygones be bygones – we've been mates for ten years, and it isn't worth falling out over something so trivial.
e: “chuyện cũ bỏ qua” = **let bygones be bygones**; “giận nhau vì” = **fall out over**. Sau “worth” dùng V-ing.
“let the past go” = **let bygones be bygones**; “argue and stop being friends over” = **fall out over**. Use -ing after “worth”.

hard.s: I'd love to come to your barbecue on Sunday, but I'm completely snowed ___ with work until the end of the month, so let's do something in July.
a: under
e: **be snowed under (with sth)** = ngập đầu (công việc). Thành ngữ thân mật rất hay dùng để từ chối lời mời một cách nhẹ nhàng.
**be snowed under (with something)** = have too much to deal with. A very common informal way to decline an invitation gently.

hard.s: I was planning to keep Mum's surprise party a secret until Sunday, but my little sister let the cat out of the box at breakfast this morning.
a: I was planning to keep Mum's surprise party a secret until Sunday, but my little sister let the cat out of the bag at breakfast this morning.
e: Thành ngữ đúng: **let the cat out of the bag** = lỡ miệng tiết lộ bí mật. Không thay “bag” bằng từ khác.
The idiom is **let the cat out of the bag** = accidentally reveal a secret. “bag” can't be replaced.
f: let the cat out of the bag

q: Viết lại cho tự nhiên, dùng thành ngữ “up in the air”.
Rewrite naturally using the idiom “up in the air”.
hard.s: We haven't decided anything about our summer holiday yet because my husband's work schedule might change.
a: Our summer holiday plans are still up in the air because my husband's work schedule might change.
Everything about our summer holiday is still up in the air because my husband's work schedule might change.
Our plans for the summer holiday are still up in the air because my husband's work schedule might change.
e: **up in the air** = chưa chắc chắn, chưa quyết. Chủ ngữ thường là “plans / everything / it”, không phải người.
**up in the air** = undecided, uncertain. The subject is usually “plans / everything / it”, not a person.

Mai: Right, let's get the ball rolling. The street party is only three weeks away, so we need to be on the same page about the budget.
Tom: Can I address the elephant in the room? Last year we bit off more than we could chew – forty stalls and only six volunteers.
Mai: You've hit the nail on the head. I don't want to cut corners on safety, though.
Tom: Agreed. And honestly, losing our big sponsor was a blessing in disguise: now we can keep it small and local.
Mai: Fair enough. Karaoke isn't really my cup of tea, but the kids love it, so it stays.

Tom: Tuyệt. Ở khu này năm thì mười họa mới có tiệc đường phố, nên phải làm cho ra trò. Hôm nay dừng ở đây nhé?

q: Năm ngoái đã xảy ra vấn đề gì?
What went wrong last year?
o: Quá nhiều gian hàng mà quá ít tình nguyện viên
Too many stalls and too few volunteers
Trời mưa nên phải hủy tiệc
It rained, so the party was cancelled
Nhà tài trợ rút lui vào phút chót
The sponsor pulled out at the last minute
e: “we bit off more than we could chew – forty stalls and only six volunteers” = ôm đồm quá sức. Nhà tài trợ là chuyện năm nay, không phải năm ngoái.
“we bit off more than we could chew – forty stalls and only six volunteers” = they took on too much. Losing the sponsor happened this year, not last year.
f: forty stalls and only six volunteers

q: Vì sao Tom gọi việc mất nhà tài trợ là “a blessing in disguise”?
Why does Tom call losing the sponsor “a blessing in disguise”?
o: Vì giờ họ có thể làm tiệc nhỏ và mang chất địa phương
Because now they can keep the party small and local
Vì họ đã tìm được nhà tài trợ lớn hơn
Because they have found a bigger sponsor
Vì nhà tài trợ đòi quá nhiều gian hàng
Because the sponsor wanted too many stalls
e: Một việc tưởng xấu (mất tài trợ) lại có kết quả tốt: “now we can keep it small and local”. Đoạn văn không nhắc nhà tài trợ mới.
Something bad (losing the sponsor) leads to something good: “now we can keep it small and local”. No new sponsor is mentioned.
f: now we can keep it small and local

q: Khi Mai nói “let's not beat around the bush”, chị muốn làm gì?
When Mai says “let's not beat around the bush”, what does she want to do?
o: Nói thẳng vấn đề: cần thêm hai tình nguyện viên trước thứ Sáu
State the problem directly: they need two more volunteers by Friday
Dọn dẹp bụi cây quanh cổng trường
Clear the bushes near the school gate
Hoãn cuộc họp sang tuần sau
Postpone the meeting until next week
e: **beat around the bush** = nói vòng vo; “let's not…” = hãy nói thẳng. Ngay sau đó chị nêu vấn đề chính. Phương án 2 là bẫy nghĩa đen.
**beat around the bush** = avoid the point; “let's not…” = let's be direct. She then states the key problem. Option 2 is the literal-meaning trap.
f: let's not beat around the bush – we need two more volunteers by Friday

ex2.s: Nobody at the residents' meeting wanted to mention that the treasurer had quit, but eventually Hoa decided to address ___ and asked who would take over the accounts.
o: the elephant in the room
the tip of the iceberg
the last straw
e: **the elephant in the room** = vấn đề hiển nhiên mà mọi người né tránh – khớp với “nobody wanted to mention”. **the tip of the iceberg** = phần nổi của tảng băng; **the last straw** = giọt nước tràn ly.

**the elephant in the room** = an obvious problem everyone avoids – matching “nobody wanted to mention”. **the tip of the iceberg** = a small visible part of a big problem; **the last straw** = the final annoyance.
f: address the elephant in the room

ex2.s: My grandmother is feeling a bit ___ today, so she won't be joining us for the morning walk, but she'd love to see everyone at dinner.
o: under the weather
over the moon
in hot water
e: **under the weather** = hơi mệt/ốm, nên bà không đi dạo được. **over the moon** = rất vui; **in hot water** = gặp rắc rối.
**under the weather** = slightly ill, so she can't go for the walk. **over the moon** = very happy; **in hot water** = in trouble.

ex2.s: We've only got two weeks until the community library opens, so if we want to finish on time we really need to get the ball ___ this afternoon.
a: rolling
e: Thành ngữ cố định **get the ball rolling** = bắt đầu một việc chung. Không dùng “running” hay “moving”.
The fixed idiom is **get the ball rolling** = start a shared activity. Not “running” or “moving”.

ex2.s: You've hit the nail on the ___: the real reason nobody volunteers is that the meetings are always held at nine o'clock on a weekday morning.
a: head
e: **hit the nail on the head** = nói trúng vấn đề, mô tả chính xác. Luôn là “the head”.
**hit the nail on the head** = describe the problem exactly. It is always “the head”.
f: hit the nail on the head

ex2.s: I know you're busy, but please stop beating around the bushes and tell me honestly whether you can help with the street party on Saturday.
a: I know you're busy, but please stop beating around the bush and tell me honestly whether you can help with the street party on Saturday.
e: Thành ngữ cố định dùng **bush** số ít: **beat around the bush** (Anh-Anh cũng nói “beat about the bush”). Đổi sang số nhiều làm câu nghe sai ngay với người bản xứ.
The fixed idiom uses singular **bush**: **beat around the bush** (British also “beat about the bush”). A plural sounds wrong to native speakers.

ex2.s: The builders clearly cut the corners to finish the community garden before the rainy season, and now half of the fences are already falling down.
a: The builders clearly cut corners to finish the community garden before the rainy season, and now half of the fences are already falling down.
e: **cut corners** = làm ẩu để tiết kiệm thời gian/tiền – không có mạo từ “the”. “cut the corner” theo nghĩa đen là đi tắt qua góc đường.
**cut corners** = do something badly to save time or money – no article. “cut the corner” literally means taking a shortcut round a bend.

ex2.s: Running five neighbourhood projects at the same time was clearly biting more than she could chew, so in the end she asked the committee for help.
a: Running five neighbourhood projects at the same time was clearly biting off more than she could chew, so in the end she asked the committee for help.
Running five neighborhood projects at the same time was clearly biting off more than she could chew, so in the end she asked the committee for help.
e: Thiếu tiểu từ: **bite OFF more than you can chew**. Cụm động từ trong thành ngữ không được bỏ tiểu từ.
The particle is missing: **bite OFF more than you can chew**. You can't drop the particle from an idiom's phrasal verb.
f: biting off more than she could chew

ex2.s: Mình biết karaoke không hợp gu bạn lắm, nhưng tối nay bạn ghé qua một lát được không, vì cả xóm đã cất công chuẩn bị rồi.
a: I know karaoke isn't really your cup of tea, but could you drop by for a bit tonight, because the whole neighbourhood has gone the extra mile to prepare?
I know karaoke isn't really your cup of tea, but could you come along for a while tonight? The whole neighbourhood has gone the extra mile to get ready.
I know karaoke's not really your cup of tea, but could you pop in for a bit tonight, since the whole street has gone to a lot of trouble to prepare?
I know karaoke isn't really your cup of tea, but could you stop by for a bit tonight, because the whole neighborhood has gone the extra mile to prepare?
e: “không hợp gu” = **not (really) my/your cup of tea** – nói mềm, không chê. “ghé qua một lát” = **drop by / pop in for a bit**; “cất công” = **go the extra mile / go to a lot of trouble**.
“not to your taste” = **not (really) your cup of tea** – soft, not critical. “come briefly” = **drop by / pop in for a bit**; “made a big effort” = **go the extra mile / go to a lot of trouble**.
f: isn't really your cup of tea

ex2.s: Hóa ra việc mất nhà tài trợ lại là trong cái rủi có cái may, vì bây giờ chúng ta có thể tổ chức lễ hội theo cách mình muốn.
a: Losing the sponsor turned out to be a blessing in disguise, because now we can organise the festival the way we want.
Losing the sponsor turned out to be a blessing in disguise, since we can now run the festival the way we want to.
It turned out that losing the sponsor was a blessing in disguise, because now we can organize the festival however we like.
e: “hóa ra” = **turned out to be / it turned out that**; “trong cái rủi có cái may” = **a blessing in disguise** (luôn có “a”). Không dịch từng chữ kiểu “luck in bad luck”.
“hóa ra” = **turned out to be / it turned out that**; “trong cái rủi có cái may” = **a blessing in disguise** (always with “a”). Don't translate word for word.
f: turned out to be a blessing in disguise

q: Viết lại câu cho tự nhiên hơn, thay “very rarely” bằng thành ngữ có “blue moon”.
Rewrite the sentence more naturally, replacing “very rarely” with an idiom containing “blue moon”.
ex2.s: My brother lives abroad, so we only see each other very rarely, usually at Tết.
a: My brother lives abroad, so we only see each other once in a blue moon, usually at Tết.
My brother lives abroad, so we see each other only once in a blue moon, usually at Tết.
e: **once in a blue moon** = rất hiếm khi (≈ năm thì mười họa). Cụm cố định: “once in a blue moon”, không nói “in the blue moon”.
**once in a blue moon** = very rarely. It's a fixed phrase: “once in a blue moon”, not “in the blue moon”.

ex2.s: Let's call it a day|and pick up|where we left off|on Monday morning,|when everyone|has had|a chance|to rest.
m: Hôm nay mình dừng ở đây và sáng thứ Hai làm tiếp từ chỗ đang dở, khi mọi người đã được nghỉ ngơi.
Let's call it a day and pick up where we left off on Monday morning, when everyone has had a chance to rest.
e: **call it a day** = dừng việc hôm nay; **pick up where we left off** = tiếp tục từ chỗ đang dở – hai cụm tự nhiên hay đi cùng nhau cuối buổi họp.
**call it a day** = stop working for today; **pick up where we left off** = continue from the same point – a natural pair at the end of a meeting.

q: Viết tin nhắn nhóm (120–150 từ) gửi nhóm chat khu phố, rủ mọi người tham gia ngày dọn dẹp công viên. Dùng tự nhiên 3–4 thành ngữ trong bài (không nhồi nhét), nêu thời gian, việc cần làm và cách đăng ký.

Write a group message (120–150 words) to your neighbourhood chat inviting people to a park clean-up day. Naturally use 3–4 idioms from this unit (don't overdo it) and give the time, the jobs and how to sign up.
ex2.m: Hi everyone! I'd like to get the ball rolling on our park clean-up, which will take place next Saturday from 7 to 10 a.m. Let's address the elephant in the room first: last time only a handful of us turned up, and we bit off more than we could chew trying to clear the whole park in two hours. So this year we're keeping it simple. We need people to pick up litter, paint the old benches and help the kids plant a few trees. Gloves, bags and cold drinks will be provided. If heavy work isn't your cup of tea, you're very welcome to help with registration or snacks instead. Please reply with your name and preferred job by Thursday evening so we're all on the same page. Thanks a million – see you there!
e: Cần có: • 3–4 thành ngữ dùng đúng dạng và đúng chỗ • thời gian, địa điểm, các việc cụ thể • cách đăng ký và hạn chót • giọng thân thiện, thân mật vừa phải.
Checklist: • 3–4 idioms in the correct form and context • time, place and specific jobs • how and when to sign up • a friendly, moderately informal tone.

t: Văn phong: trang trọng – trung tính – thân mật
th:
**Ngữ pháp 1 – Cùng một ý, ba văn phong**
• Trang trọng: **I would be grateful if you could** send me the report by Friday.
• Trung tính: **Could you** send me the report by Friday, please?
• Thân mật: **Can you send** the report **over** by Friday?
Xin lỗi: **We sincerely apologise for any inconvenience.** → **Sorry for the delay.** → **Sorry – my bad!**
Hoãn họp: **The meeting has been postponed.** → **The meeting has been moved to Thursday.** → **Meeting's been put off till Thursday.**

**Grammar 1 – One message, three registers**
• Formal: **I would be grateful if you could** send me the report by Friday.
• Neutral: **Could you** send me the report by Friday, please?
• Informal: **Can you send** the report **over** by Friday?
Apologising: **We sincerely apologise for any inconvenience.** → **Sorry for the delay.** → **Sorry – my bad!**
Moving a meeting: **The meeting has been postponed.** → **The meeting has been moved to Thursday.** → **Meeting's been put off till Thursday.**

**Ngữ pháp 2 – Dấu hiệu của từng văn phong**
• **Trang trọng**: động từ gốc Latin (inform, require, assist, obtain, commence, enquire, purchase), bị động (The order **has been dispatched**), danh từ hóa (**the delivery of** your order), đảo ngữ **Should you require…** (= If you need…), không viết tắt.
• **Trung tính**: động từ thường ngày (tell, need, help, get, start, ask, buy), câu hỏi lịch sự **Could we…?**, có thể viết tắt.
• **Thân mật**: cụm động từ (**let sb know, sort out, held up, put off**), viết tắt, lược từ (**Client's been told.** / **Fancy a coffee?**), thán từ (Ugh, Hey).
• Lỗi hay gặp: trộn văn phong – “Hey Mr Smith, I would be grateful…” hay “Dear Professor, can you give me a hand?”.

**Grammar 2 – Markers of each register**
• **Formal**: Latin-based verbs (inform, require, assist, obtain, commence, enquire, purchase), passives (The order **has been dispatched**), nominalisation (**the delivery of** your order), inversion **Should you require…** (= If you need…), no contractions.
• **Neutral**: everyday verbs (tell, need, help, get, start, ask, buy), polite questions **Could we…?**, contractions are fine.
• **Informal**: phrasal verbs (**let sb know, sort out, held up, put off**), contractions, ellipsis (**Client's been told.** / **Fancy a coffee?**), interjections (Ugh, Hey).
• Common mistake: mixing registers – “Hey Mr Smith, I would be grateful…” or “Dear Professor, can you give me a hand?”.

**Mở đầu & kết thư theo văn phong (Anh-Anh)**
• Không biết tên: **Dear Sir or Madam,** … **Yours faithfully,**
• Biết tên, trang trọng: **Dear Ms Grant,** … **Yours sincerely, / Kind regards,** (dùng họ, KHÔNG “Dear Ms Linda”).
• Trung tính, đồng nghiệp: **Hi David,** … **Best, / Best wishes,**
• Thân mật: **Hey Sam!** … **Cheers, / See you soon,**
• Câu chuyển tiếp: **I am writing to enquire about…** (trang trọng) – **Just a quick note about…** (trung tính) – **Quick question:** (thân mật).

**Openings & closings by register (British usage)**
• Name unknown: **Dear Sir or Madam,** … **Yours faithfully,**
• Name known, formal: **Dear Ms Grant,** … **Yours sincerely, / Kind regards,** (use the surname, NOT “Dear Ms Linda”).
• Neutral, colleagues: **Hi David,** … **Best, / Best wishes,**
• Informal: **Hey Sam!** … **Cheers, / See you soon,**
• Opening lines: **I am writing to enquire about…** (formal) – **Just a quick note about…** (neutral) – **Quick question:** (informal).

**Phát âm – Văn phong cũng nghe thấy được**
• Trang trọng (thuyết trình, gọi khách hàng): nói dạng đầy đủ **I would / we have**, tốc độ vừa phải, xuống giọng rõ cuối câu.
• Thân mật: dạng rút gọn và âm yếu: **I'd, we've, gonna /ˈɡʌn.ə/, wanna /ˈwɑː.nə/** – chỉ dùng khi NÓI, không viết trong email công việc.
• **Fancy a coffee?** lên giọng ở cuối ↗; **We regret to inform you…** đều đều, nghiêm túc.
• Từ khó: enquire /ɪnˈkwaɪr/, inconvenience /ˌɪn.kənˈviː.ni.əns/, faithfully /ˈfeɪθ.fəl.i/, regards /rɪˈɡɑːrdz/.

**Pronunciation – You can hear register too**
• Formal (presentations, client calls): full forms **I would / we have**, a moderate pace, clear falling tones at the end.
• Informal: contractions and weak forms: **I'd, we've, gonna /ˈɡʌn.ə/, wanna /ˈwɑː.nə/** – only in SPEECH, never in work emails.
• **Fancy a coffee?** rises at the end ↗; **We regret to inform you…** is even and serious.
• Tricky words: enquire /ɪnˈkwaɪr/, inconvenience /ˌɪn.kənˈviː.ni.əns/, faithfully /ˈfeɪθ.fəl.i/, regards /rɪˈɡɑːrdz/.

**Tự luyện ngoài app**
• Nghe (20 phút): nghe 1 cuộc gọi chăm sóc khách hàng và 1 vlog, ghi 5 cụm trang trọng & 5 cụm thân mật.
• Nói (20 phút): đóng vai báo một tin xấu (hủy chuyến, trễ hàng) 3 lần: cho khách hàng, cho sếp, cho bạn thân.
• Đọc (20 phút): đọc 2 email thật (thư thông báo của ngân hàng & tin nhắn nhóm bạn), gạch chân dấu hiệu văn phong.
• Viết (30 phút): viết lại một email của bạn theo 2 văn phong khác nhau.
• Từ vựng (15 phút): lập bảng cặp từ trang trọng ↔ thường ngày: inform/tell, require/need, assist/help, obtain/get, commence/start, purchase/buy, postpone/put off.

**Practice outside the app**
• Listening (20 min): listen to a customer-service call and a vlog; note 5 formal and 5 informal phrases.
• Speaking (20 min): role-play giving bad news (a cancelled trip, a late delivery) three times: to a client, a boss and a close friend.
• Reading (20 min): read 2 real messages (a bank notice and a friends' group chat) and underline the register markers.
• Writing (30 min): rewrite one of your own emails in 2 different registers.
• Vocabulary (15 min): build a table of formal ↔ everyday pairs: inform/tell, require/need, assist/help, obtain/get, commence/start, purchase/buy, postpone/put off.
