warm.s: Should you require any further assistance with your booking, please do not hesitate to contact our customer service team at any time.
q: Câu này thuộc văn phong nào và thực chất muốn nói gì?
What register is this and what does it actually mean?
o: Trang trọng – “Nếu cần giúp thêm thì cứ liên hệ chúng tôi”
Formal – “If you need more help, just contact us”
Thân mật – “Đừng gọi cho chúng tôi nữa”
Informal – “Don't call us again”
Trung tính – “Bạn bắt buộc phải liên hệ chúng tôi”
Neutral – “You must contact us”
e: Đảo ngữ **Should you require…** (= If you need…) và **do not hesitate to** là dấu hiệu thư trang trọng. “do not hesitate” = cứ tự nhiên, không phải lệnh cấm hay bắt buộc.
The inversion **Should you require…** (= If you need…) and **do not hesitate to** mark formal writing. “do not hesitate” = feel free, not a ban or an obligation.
f: Should you require any further assistance

warm.s: I would be grateful if you could send me the updated figures by Friday, as I need them for the board meeting.
e: Khung trang trọng **I would be grateful if you could + V**; “as” = because (trang trọng hơn). Không viết tắt “I'd” trong thư trang trọng.
The formal frame **I would be grateful if you could + verb**; “as” = because (more formal). Don't contract to “I'd” in formal writing.
f: I would be grateful if you could

warm.s: Hi Sam, just a quick update: the delivery's been held up, so could we push the meeting back to Thursday afternoon?
e: Văn phong trung tính-thân mật: đọc nhanh, nối âm “delivery's been”, “push the meeting back”; lên giọng nhẹ ở câu hỏi cuối.
Neutral-to-informal: keep it quick, link “delivery's been” and “push the meeting back”; let the final question rise slightly.

warm.s: We sincerely apologise for any inconvenience this may cause and will keep you informed of any further developments.
e: Văn phong trang trọng: đọc chậm, đầy đủ, nhấn in-con-**VEN**-ience và de-**VEL**-opments, xuống giọng dứt khoát cuối câu.
Formal register: speak slowly and fully, stress in-con-**VEN**-ience and de-**VEL**-opments, and end with a firm fall.

q: Câu ra lệnh này nghe cộc lốc với hàng xóm. Viết lại thành lời nhờ lịch sự bắt đầu bằng “Would you mind…”.
This order sounds rude to a neighbour. Rewrite it as a polite request beginning “Would you mind…”.
hard.s: Move your car, it's blocking my gate and I need to take my son to school.
a: Would you mind moving your car? It's blocking my gate and I need to take my son to school.
Would you mind moving your car, please? It's blocking my gate and I need to take my son to school.
Would you mind moving your car? It's blocking my gate, and I need to take my son to school.
e: **Would you mind + V-ing?** là lời nhờ lịch sự, vừa phải – hợp với hàng xóm. Sau “mind” dùng V-ing (moving), không dùng “to move”.
**Would you mind + -ing?** is a polite, neutral request – right for a neighbour. Use -ing after “mind” (moving), not “to move”.
f: Would you mind moving your car

hard.s: Chị ơi, hôm nay em xin phép về sớm một chút được không ạ – con em bị sốt, em hứa tối mai sẽ làm bù.
a: Would it be all right if I left a bit early today? My son's running a temperature, and I promise I'll make up the time tomorrow evening.
Would it be OK if I left a little early today? My son has a fever, and I promise I'll make up the hours tomorrow evening.
Do you think I could leave a bit early today? My daughter's got a temperature, and I promise to make up the time tomorrow evening.
e: “xin phép” với sếp → **Would it be all right if I + quá khứ (left)…?** (quá khứ giả định cho lịch sự). “làm bù” = **make up the time**; “bị sốt” = **be running a temperature / have a fever**.
Asking a boss's permission → **Would it be all right if I + past (left)…?** (the past adds politeness). “work the hours later” = **make up the time**; “have a fever” = **be running a temperature**.
f: Would it be all right if I left a bit early

hard.s: Sorry to be a pain, but would you mind ___ the music down a little? My little one has only just gone to sleep and the walls here are really thin.
a: turning
e: **turn the music down** = vặn nhỏ nhạc; sau **would you mind** dùng V-ing → **turning**. “Sorry to be a pain” = xin lỗi vì làm phiền (thân mật, mềm mỏng).
**turn the music down** = make it quieter; after **would you mind** use -ing → **turning**. “Sorry to be a pain” is a soft, informal apology for bothering someone.
f: would you mind turning the music down

hard.s: Hey mate, I regret to inform you that I can't make it to football tonight – I've got loads of work on, but I'll definitely be there next week.
a: Hey mate, sorry, I can't make it to football tonight – I've got loads of work on, but I'll definitely be there next week.
Hey mate, I'm afraid I can't make it to football tonight – I've got loads of work on, but I'll definitely be there next week.
Hey mate, sorry but I can't make it to football tonight – I've got loads of work on, but I'll definitely be there next week.
e: **I regret to inform you** quá trang trọng cho tin nhắn bạn bè – nghe như đùa hoặc lạnh lùng. Dùng **sorry** hoặc **I'm afraid**.
**I regret to inform you** is far too formal for a text to a friend – it sounds sarcastic or cold. Use **sorry** or **I'm afraid**.
f: I'm afraid I can't make it

rd2.tx:
Message 1 – to a client (formal)
Dear Ms Grant,
We regret to inform you that, owing to unforeseen circumstances at our supplier, the delivery of your order has been postponed until 14 May. We sincerely apologise for any inconvenience this may cause. Should you require any further information, please do not hesitate to contact me.
Yours sincerely,
Linh Tran, Account Manager

Message 2 – to her manager (neutral)
Hi David,
Just a quick update: our supplier has had some problems, so the Grant order is going to be about a week late. I've already let the client know and apologised. Could we discuss offering them a small discount at Monday's meeting?
Best,
Linh

Message 3 – to a colleague (informal)
Ugh, the Grant order's been held up again – the supplier messed up. Client's been told, though. Fancy grabbing a coffee later and sorting out a plan B?
rd2.tr:
Tin 1 – gửi khách hàng (trang trọng)
Kính gửi bà Grant,
Chúng tôi rất tiếc phải thông báo rằng, do những tình huống bất khả kháng tại nhà cung cấp, việc giao đơn hàng của bà đã được hoãn đến ngày 14 tháng 5. Chúng tôi thành thật xin lỗi vì mọi sự bất tiện có thể gây ra. Nếu bà cần thêm thông tin, xin đừng ngần ngại liên hệ với tôi.
Trân trọng,
Trần Linh, Quản lý khách hàng

Tin 2 – gửi quản lý (trung tính)
Chào anh David,
Em cập nhật nhanh: nhà cung cấp gặp chút trục trặc nên đơn hàng của bà Grant sẽ trễ khoảng một tuần. Em đã báo và xin lỗi khách rồi. Mình có thể bàn việc giảm giá nhẹ cho họ trong cuộc họp thứ Hai không ạ?
Thân,
Linh

Tin 3 – gửi đồng nghiệp (thân mật)
Trời ơi, đơn của bà Grant lại bị kẹt nữa rồi – bên cung cấp làm hỏng việc. Nhưng đã báo khách rồi. Lát đi cà phê rồi tính phương án B không?

q: Vì sao đơn hàng bị trễ?
Why is the order late?
o: Nhà cung cấp gặp sự cố ngoài dự kiến
The supplier had unexpected problems
Khách hàng đổi địa chỉ giao hàng
The client changed the delivery address
Linh quên gửi đơn hàng
Linh forgot to send the order
e: Cùng một lý do được nói theo 3 cách: “owing to unforeseen circumstances at our supplier” (trang trọng) – “our supplier has had some problems” (trung tính) – “the supplier messed up” (thân mật).
The same reason in three registers: “owing to unforeseen circumstances at our supplier” (formal) – “our supplier has had some problems” (neutral) – “the supplier messed up” (informal).
f: owing to unforeseen circumstances at our supplier

q: Linh đề nghị gì với quản lý?
What does Linh suggest to her manager?
o: Bàn việc giảm giá nhỏ cho khách trong cuộc họp thứ Hai
Discussing a small discount for the client at Monday's meeting
Đổi sang nhà cung cấp khác ngay lập tức
Changing suppliers immediately
Gọi điện xin lỗi khách thêm lần nữa
Calling the client to apologise again
e: “Could we discuss offering them a small discount at Monday's meeting?” – câu hỏi lịch sự trung tính với Could we. Linh đã xin lỗi khách rồi (“I've already… apologised”).
“Could we discuss offering them a small discount at Monday's meeting?” – a neutral polite question with Could we. She has already apologised to the client.
f: Could we discuss offering them a small discount

q: Đặc điểm nào cho thấy Tin 3 là văn phong thân mật?
Which features show that Message 3 is informal?
o: Thán từ, cụm động từ và câu lược chủ ngữ/trợ từ
An interjection, phrasal verbs and missing words
Câu bị động dài và đảo ngữ
Long passive sentences and inversion
Lời chào và lời kết đầy đủ
A full greeting and closing
e: “Ugh” (thán từ), “held up / messed up / sorting out” (cụm động từ), “Client's been told” và “Fancy grabbing…?” (lược “The”, “Do you”). Tin 3 không có lời chào/kết.
“Ugh” (interjection), “held up / messed up / sorting out” (phrasal verbs), “Client's been told” and “Fancy grabbing…?” (missing “The”, “Do you”). It has no greeting or closing.
f: Client's been told, though. Fancy grabbing a coffee later

ex2.s: Dear Mr Patel, I am writing to ___ about the availability of your conference rooms for a two-day training event that our company is planning in early June.
o: enquire
ask around
check out
e: Thư trang trọng mở bằng **I am writing to enquire about…** (Mỹ: inquire). **ask around** = hỏi quanh mọi người, **check out** = xem thử – đều thân mật, không hợp với “Dear Mr Patel”.
Formal letters open with **I am writing to enquire about…** (US: inquire). **ask around** and **check out** are informal and clash with “Dear Mr Patel”.
f: I am writing to enquire about

ex2.s: Sorry I can't make it tonight – something's come up at work – but shall we just ___ till Friday and grab dinner after the gym instead?
o: put it off
postpone it
defer it
e: Tin nhắn cho bạn bè dùng cụm động từ thân mật **put it off**. **postpone** (trung tính-trang trọng) và **defer** (rất trang trọng, hành chính) nghe cứng nhắc trong tin nhắn này.
A text to a friend calls for the informal phrasal verb **put it off**. **postpone** (neutral-formal) and **defer** (very formal, official) sound stiff here.

ex2.s: We regret to ___ you that, due to essential maintenance work, the office car park will be closed to all staff from Monday to Friday next week.
a: inform
e: Công thức thông báo tin xấu trang trọng: **We regret to inform you that…** Không dùng “tell” trong khung này.
The formal formula for bad news: **We regret to inform you that…** “tell” doesn't fit this frame.
f: We regret to inform you that

ex2.s: ___ you have any questions about your new contract, please do not hesitate to contact the Human Resources department, which is open from nine until five.
a: Should
e: Đảo ngữ trang trọng **Should you + V** = If you + V. Động từ sau “you” ở dạng nguyên thể (have, require), không chia.
Formal inversion **Should you + verb** = If you + verb. The verb after “you” stays in the base form (have, require).

ex2.s: Dear Professor Nguyen, I am writing to ask whether you could give me a hand with my thesis proposal, which I need to submit to the faculty before the end of this month.
a: Dear Professor Nguyen, I am writing to ask whether you could help me with my thesis proposal, which I need to submit to the faculty before the end of this month.
Dear Professor Nguyen, I am writing to ask whether you could assist me with my thesis proposal, which I need to submit to the faculty before the end of this month.
e: Lỗi trộn văn phong: **give me a hand** là thân mật, lạc lõng trong thư gửi giáo sư. Dùng **help me** (trung tính) hoặc **assist me** (trang trọng).
A register clash: **give me a hand** is informal and out of place in a letter to a professor. Use **help me** (neutral) or **assist me** (formal).

ex2.s: Because I didn't know the manager's name, I opened my complaint letter with “Dear Sir or Madam” and closed it with “Yours sincerely” before posting it.
a: Because I didn't know the manager's name, I opened my complaint letter with “Dear Sir or Madam” and closed it with “Yours faithfully” before posting it.
e: Theo quy ước Anh-Anh: **Dear Sir or Madam** (không biết tên) → **Yours faithfully**; **Dear Ms/Mr + họ** → **Yours sincerely**. (Tiếng Anh-Mỹ thường dùng “Sincerely” cho cả hai.)
British convention: **Dear Sir or Madam** (name unknown) → **Yours faithfully**; **Dear Ms/Mr + surname** → **Yours sincerely**. (American English usually uses “Sincerely” for both.)

ex2.s: Should you requiring any further information about the course, please contact the admissions office directly rather than replying to this automated email.
a: Should you require any further information about the course, please contact the admissions office directly rather than replying to this automated email.
e: Sau đảo ngữ **Should you** dùng động từ nguyên thể: **Should you require**, không phải “requiring”.
After the inversion **Should you** use the base verb: **Should you require**, not “requiring”.

ex2.s: Chúng tôi thành thật xin lỗi vì mọi sự bất tiện mà việc chậm trễ này có thể gây ra và sẽ thông báo cho quý khách ngay khi đơn hàng được gửi đi.
a: We sincerely apologise for any inconvenience this delay may cause and will inform you as soon as your order has been dispatched.
We sincerely apologise for any inconvenience that this delay may cause, and we will inform you as soon as your order has been dispatched.
We sincerely apologize for any inconvenience this delay may cause and will notify you as soon as your order has been shipped.
We sincerely apologise for any inconvenience caused by this delay and will inform you as soon as your order has been dispatched.
e: Văn phong trang trọng: **sincerely apologise for any inconvenience**, **inform/notify** (không “let you know”), bị động **has been dispatched**. “quý khách” chỉ cần “you”.
Formal register: **sincerely apologise for any inconvenience**, **inform/notify** (not “let you know”), the passive **has been dispatched**. “quý khách” is simply “you”.
f: We sincerely apologise for any inconvenience

ex2.s: Ê, cuộc họp chiều nay bị lùi sang thứ Năm rồi, nên tối nay đi ăn gì đó rồi tính nốt kế hoạch cho chuyến đi không?
a: Hey, this afternoon's meeting has been pushed back to Thursday, so fancy grabbing something to eat tonight and sorting out the rest of the plan for the trip?
Hey, this afternoon's meeting's been put off till Thursday, so do you fancy grabbing a bite tonight and sorting out the rest of the trip plan?
Hey, the meeting this afternoon has been moved to Thursday, so want to grab something to eat tonight and finish sorting out the plan for the trip?
e: Tin nhắn bạn bè → thân mật: **pushed back / put off** (không “postponed”), **fancy + V-ing?**, **grab something to eat / a bite**, **sort out**.
A text to a friend → informal: **pushed back / put off** (not “postponed”), **fancy + -ing?**, **grab something to eat / a bite**, **sort out**.

q: Viết lại câu hỏi thân mật thành câu yêu cầu trang trọng bắt đầu bằng “I would be grateful if…”.
Rewrite the informal question as a formal request beginning “I would be grateful if…”.
ex2.s: Can you send over the signed contract by Friday?
a: I would be grateful if you could send me the signed contract by Friday.
I would be grateful if you could send the signed contract by Friday.
I would be grateful if you would send me the signed contract by Friday.
e: **I would be grateful if you could/would + V** là lời yêu cầu trang trọng chuẩn. Bỏ cụm động từ thân mật “send over” → **send (me)**.
**I would be grateful if you could/would + verb** is the standard formal request. Replace the informal phrasal verb “send over” with **send (me)**.
f: I would be grateful if you could send

q: Viết lại thông báo trang trọng thành tin nhắn thân mật cho đồng nghiệp thân, dùng “put off” và “something's come up”.
Rewrite the formal notice as an informal text to a close colleague, using “put off” and “something's come up”.
ex2.s: The meeting has been postponed owing to unforeseen circumstances.
a: The meeting's been put off – something's come up.
Meeting's been put off – something's come up.
The meeting has been put off because something's come up.
e: **postponed** → **put off**; **owing to unforeseen circumstances** → **something's come up** (có việc đột xuất). Văn phong thân mật thích viết tắt và lược từ.
**postponed** → **put off**; **owing to unforeseen circumstances** → **something's come up**. Informal style likes contractions and ellipsis.
f: The meeting's been put off – something's come up

ex2.s: I would be grateful|if you could|let me know|whether the dates|we discussed|are still convenient|for your team.
m: Tôi sẽ rất biết ơn nếu anh/chị có thể cho tôi biết liệu những ngày chúng ta đã bàn có còn thuận tiện cho nhóm của anh/chị không.
I would be grateful if you could let me know whether the dates we discussed are still convenient for your team.
e: Khung trang trọng **I would be grateful if you could…** + câu hỏi gián tiếp **whether…** (trật tự chủ ngữ – động từ như câu kể).
The formal frame **I would be grateful if you could…** + an indirect question **whether…** (statement word order).
f: I would be grateful if you could let me know whether

q: Viết CÙNG một tin theo 2 văn phong: (1) email trang trọng (70–90 từ) gửi khách sạn xin đổi ngày đặt phòng vì lịch công tác thay đổi; (2) tin nhắn thân mật (30–40 từ) báo bạn thân rằng chuyến đi bị dời.

Write the SAME news in 2 registers: (1) a formal email (70–90 words) to a hotel asking to change your booking dates because your business trip has changed; (2) an informal text (30–40 words) telling a close friend the trip has moved.
ex2.m:
(1) Dear Sir or Madam,
I am writing with regard to my reservation (booking reference HN2048) for a double room from 10 to 13 June. Owing to a change in my business schedule, I would be grateful if you could amend the booking to 17–20 June. Should the room not be available on these dates, please let me know what alternatives you can offer. I apologise for any inconvenience and look forward to hearing from you.
Yours faithfully,
Linh Tran

(2) Hey Mai! Bad news – work's messed up my plans again, so the Hanoi trip's been pushed back a week, to the 17th. Still up for that street-food tour? Let me know and I'll sort out the tickets!
e: Cần có: • Bản 1: lời chào/kết đúng cặp, lý do bằng danh từ (owing to…), yêu cầu với “I would be grateful if…”, không viết tắt • Bản 2: cụm động từ, viết tắt, câu ngắn, giọng thân thiện • Thông tin hai bản khớp nhau.

Checklist: • Version 1: matching greeting/closing, a noun-based reason (owing to…), a request with “I would be grateful if…”, no contractions • Version 2: phrasal verbs, contractions, short sentences, a friendly tone • The facts match in both versions.

t: Bài đọc: Nghịch lý của sự lựa chọn

rd.tx: In the supermarket aisle, faced with forty varieties of jam, most of us assume that more options can only be a good thing. Yet a number of psychologists have argued that an abundance of choice may actually undermine our satisfaction. When options multiply, so does the effort required to compare them, and so does the nagging suspicion that a better alternative was left on the shelf. Some studies found that shoppers offered a smaller selection were more likely to buy anything at all. That said, later attempts to replicate these findings have produced mixed results, suggesting that the effect depends heavily on context: how much people already know, how similar the options are, and how much the decision matters to them. What seems clear is that choice is not an unqualified good; beyond a certain point, it can become a burden rather than a freedom.
rd.tr: Đứng giữa lối đi trong siêu thị trước bốn mươi loại mứt, phần lớn chúng ta cho rằng nhiều lựa chọn hơn chỉ có thể là điều tốt. Thế nhưng một số nhà tâm lý học cho rằng quá nhiều lựa chọn có thể làm giảm sự hài lòng. Khi lựa chọn tăng lên, công sức so sánh cũng tăng, và cả cảm giác day dứt rằng một lựa chọn tốt hơn đã bị bỏ lại trên kệ. Một số nghiên cứu thấy người mua được đưa ít lựa chọn hơn lại dễ mua hàng hơn. Tuy vậy, những lần làm lại các nghiên cứu này cho kết quả không thống nhất, cho thấy hiệu ứng phụ thuộc nhiều vào bối cảnh: người ta đã hiểu biết đến đâu, các lựa chọn giống nhau đến mức nào, và quyết định quan trọng với họ ra sao. Điều có vẻ rõ ràng là lựa chọn không phải lúc nào cũng tốt; vượt quá một ngưỡng, nó có thể thành gánh nặng thay vì tự do.

ex: Nhiều lựa chọn có thể làm giảm sự hài lòng
Người ta luôn mua nhiều hơn

context, such as knowledge and how much the decision matters

warm.s: When options multiply, so does the effort required to compare them, and so does the nagging suspicion that we have chosen badly.
q: Điều gì tăng lên cùng với số lựa chọn?
What increases along with the number of options?
o: Công sức so sánh và nỗi nghi ngờ đã chọn sai
The effort to compare and the doubt about our choice
Giá của sản phẩm
The price of the products
Sự hài lòng với lựa chọn cuối cùng
Our satisfaction with the final choice
e: Cấu trúc đảo “so does + chủ ngữ” = cái đó cũng tăng theo. Hai thứ tăng theo là effort và nagging suspicion; sự hài lòng thì ngược lại, giảm đi.
The inversion “so does + subject” = that increases too. The two things that grow are the effort and the nagging suspicion; satisfaction actually falls.
f: so does the effort required to compare them

warm.s: Later attempts to replicate these findings have produced mixed results, suggesting that the effect depends heavily on context.
e: Chú ý chính tả replicate và cụm phân từ “suggesting that…” nối tiếp ý của mệnh đề chính.
Note the spelling of replicate and the participle clause “suggesting that…”, which continues the main clause.

warm.s: Beyond a certain point, an abundance of choice can become a burden rather than a freedom, especially when the decision really matters.
e: Đọc nối “an abundance of”; nhấn a-BUN-dance và BUR-den. Đối lập “a burden rather than a freedom” cần nhấn cả hai danh từ.
Link “an abundance of”; stress a-BUN-dance and BUR-den. In the contrast “a burden rather than a freedom”, stress both nouns.

ex2.s: As the number of streaming services grows, so ___ the time viewers spend scrolling through menus before they finally pick something to watch.
o: does
do
is
e: “so + trợ động từ + chủ ngữ” = cũng vậy. Chủ ngữ the time là số ít và động từ gốc grows ở hiện tại đơn → so does. Đây chính là mẫu “so does the effort” trong bài đọc.
“so + auxiliary + subject” = likewise. The subject the time is singular and the verb grows is present simple → so does. It mirrors “so does the effort” in the passage.

ex2.s: Psychologists have argued that an abundance of choice may actually ___ our satisfaction, because we keep wondering what we have missed.
a: undermine
reduce
decrease
lower
diminish
e: undermine = làm suy yếu dần (từ trong bài). Cũng chấp nhận reduce, lower, diminish. Sau may dùng động từ nguyên mẫu, không thêm -s.
undermine = gradually weaken (the word in the text); reduce, lower and diminish are also accepted. After may use the base form, with no -s.

ex2.s: Some studies found that shoppers which were offered a smaller selection were more likely to buy anything at all than those facing forty options.
a: Some studies found that shoppers who were offered a smaller selection were more likely to buy anything at all than those facing forty options.
Some studies found that shoppers offered a smaller selection were more likely to buy anything at all than those facing forty options.
Some studies found that shoppers that were offered a smaller selection were more likely to buy anything at all than those facing forty options.
e: shoppers là người → who (hoặc that), không dùng which. Bài đọc dùng dạng rút gọn “shoppers offered a smaller selection”, cũng hoàn toàn đúng.
shoppers are people → who (or that), not which. The passage uses the reduced form “shoppers offered a smaller selection”, which is also correct.

q: Viết lại câu bằng câu chẻ “What seems clear is…”
Rewrite the sentence using the cleft “What seems clear is…”
ex2.s: Clearly, choice is not an unqualified good, and beyond a certain point it can become a burden rather than a freedom.
a: What seems clear is that choice is not an unqualified good, and beyond a certain point it can become a burden rather than a freedom.
What seems clear is that choice is not an unqualified good; beyond a certain point, it can become a burden rather than a freedom.
What seems clear is that choice is not an unqualified good, and that beyond a certain point it can become a burden rather than a freedom.
e: Trạng từ Clearly chuyển thành What-cleft: What seems clear is that + mệnh đề. Đừng quên that sau is.
The adverb Clearly becomes a what-cleft: What seems clear is that + clause. Don't forget that after is.

ex2.s: Hiệu ứng này dường như phụ thuộc rất nhiều vào bối cảnh, chẳng hạn người mua đã hiểu biết đến đâu và quyết định đó quan trọng với họ ra sao.
a: This effect seems to depend heavily on context, such as how much shoppers already know and how much the decision matters to them.
This effect appears to depend heavily on context, for example how much buyers already know and how important the decision is to them.
The effect seems to depend largely on context, such as how much consumers already know and how much the decision matters to them.
e: “dường như” → seems / appears to + V. Hai câu hỏi gián tiếp (how much shoppers already know, how much the decision matters) giữ trật tự câu khẳng định, như trong bài đọc.
“dường như” → seems / appears to + V. The two embedded questions (how much shoppers already know, how much the decision matters) keep statement word order, as in the passage.
f: seems to depend heavily on context

ex2.s: Faced with|forty varieties|of jam,|most of us|assume that|more options|can only be|a good thing.
m: Đứng trước bốn mươi loại mứt, phần lớn chúng ta cho rằng nhiều lựa chọn hơn chỉ có thể là điều tốt.
Faced with forty varieties of jam, most of us assume that more options can only be a good thing.
e: Cụm phân từ quá khứ “Faced with…” đứng đầu câu, có chủ ngữ ngầm là most of us. Không viết “Facing with”.
The past participle clause “Faced with…” opens the sentence; its implied subject is most of us. Don't write “Facing with”.
